sections.h2: Which McKee offices handle your tax bill
sections.html:
Property tax in this rural county runs through three offices in McKee. One values the land, one collects the money and one keeps the deed books.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7634, fax (606) 287-7079. It keeps property records and assesses property.
  • Sheriff: P.O. Box 426, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7121. Collecting taxes is the first item in its duties.
  • County Clerk: P.O. Box 339, McKee, KY 40447, phone (606) 287-7800. Land records, meaning deeds and mortgages, plus transfers, are filed here.

Call the Sheriff to learn which payment methods and counter hours apply.

The statewide calendar applies. Under KRS 134.015 the bill is due by December 31, and paying everything by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount.

A late mailing can lead Revenue to set an alternative schedule with a month per stage. The Sheriff's collecting ends April 15, after which the Clerk holds whatever is unpaid. If your bill never arrives, phone the Sheriff, because a lost bill doesn't cancel a penalty.

The first move is a conference with the PVA. KRS 133.120 makes it a required first step, held before or during the inspection period, and a telephone conference is available on request.

Still unsatisfied afterward? Mail or deliver a written petition to the County Clerk naming the parcel and your reasons and stating what you think fair cash value is. It must arrive one workday after the inspection period closes. Plan ahead, since the bill itself comes too late to contest.

A public hearing before the board of assessment appeals comes next. Collect these beforehand:

  • A description of the land and buildings.
  • Insurance policies and construction costs.
  • Listings, contracts or a recent appraisal.
  • Loan or mortgage papers on the parcel.

A petition without supporting facts can be denied. During the case, tax stays payable on your claimed value.

The deduction is $49,100 off the assessment for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. In a county where the middle home value is $111,500, that is a large share of the taxable base.

Applicants need to be 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement-system program, and live in the house. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport shown at the PVA proves age. Disability claims renew yearly, with exceptions for service-connected disabilities and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

The deduction attaches to the owner's own residence. After you move, tell the PVA and file again for the new address.

Plan to settle it from your sale proceeds. The tax is a personal debt dating from the assessment date, the lien on the land can last 11 years, and at the April 15 cutoff the Clerk files the bill as a certificate of delinquency.

After that the clock runs fast. A County Attorney notice goes out within 30 days of transfer, with a second within 60 if needed. KRS 134.128 sets the tax sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and the Clerk advertises the list 30 to 45 days before it. Commissions and interest are added along the way, so ask the Jackson County Clerk at (606) 287-7800 for the real payoff.

Get that figure in writing before you sign a listing agreement, and give it to the title company so it can pay the Clerk from your proceeds.

sections.h2: Recording a deed and the transfer tax
sections.html:
The County Clerk in McKee records deeds. The same office issues vehicle and marriage licenses, keeps wills and notary bonds, and collects the state transfer tax before taking a deed.

KRS 142.050 bills the grantor 50 cents per $500 of value. Gifts with nominal value, divorcing spouses and foreclosure transfers are among the exempt cases.

Ask the Clerk for the current recording fee before closing, since the statute sets that amount and lawmakers can change it.

sections.h2: Jackson County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Jackson County has 13,325 residents, a 2.8 percent gain since 2020. Owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes. The middle home value is $111,500, median gross rent is $665 and median household income is $40,000. The mean commute is 37.7 minutes.

Monthly owner costs are $1,101 with a mortgage and $355 without, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Sellers here are almost always dealing with an existing house, and the assessment on it traces back to the PVA's January 1 value.

McKee is the county seat and Annville is the largest community. Three industrial parks, in Annville, McKee and Sandgap, anchor local jobs.

sections.h2: What to bring to the offices
sections.html:
Before you list, collect your last tax bill and the deed. If you plan to dispute a value, add photos, an appraisal or comparable sales. For the homestead exemption, bring proof of age. Mail takes time in a rural county, so phone first and ask whether the office wants originals or copies.

At closing, the title company usually handles the recording trip. Confirm with the Clerk that the transfer tax and recording fee will be collected when the deed is filed, and keep the receipt.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jackson County PVA?
faqs.a: Write to P.O. Box 249, McKee, KY 40447, or call (606) 287-7634. Fax goes to (606) 287-7079.

faqs.q: What is the discount for paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent off, provided the full bill is paid by November 1 as KRS 134.015 allows. Afterward the amount on the bill applies until the year ends.

faqs.q: What does a late payment cost?
faqs.a: The statute adds 5 percent during January and 10 percent after that. A bill unpaid at the April 15 cutoff moves to the Clerk, where monthly interest of 1 percent and commissions begin.

faqs.q: Can a seller keep the homestead exemption after leaving?
faqs.a: No. The exemption covers the home the owner lives in, so after closing the seller tells the PVA and files again for the new residence.

faqs.q: Is the deed recorded at the McKee courthouse?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk there files deeds and mortgages and collects the transfer tax of 50 cents per $500. Phone (606) 287-7800 to confirm current fees.
